title: Selective sync: replicas of some collections
description:
The task widget only ever shows tasks, but its replica holds every note the user has ever written, and notes are by far the larger collection. This lets a replica keep only some collections. It is done entirely in the client: the server still sends the whole feed, and the client skips what it does not keep.

- `SyncClient.open({ collections })` takes the collections the replica keeps (known names, each once, at least one; otherwise a `RangeError`). The set is stored in `meta` (`collections`); opening without the option keeps the stored set, and replicas created before keep everything as they do today.
- `get`, `list`, `set` and `setMany` on another collection throw `CollectionNotKeptError` (`collection_not_kept`) before anything is written.
- Pull skips the events of collections the replica does not keep, reading the set in the same transaction as the page, and the cursor still moves past them. Events of a collection the client does not know at all still fail the page, as before.
- Opening an existing replica with a different set: collections left out lose their local documents in the open transaction (their unpushed writes stay in the outbox and are pushed as usual); added collections become pending (`collections()` returns `{ kept, pending }`) because the cursor is already past their events. A pending collection cannot be read or written until `resync()`.
- `resync()` is a sync that, after pushing, pulls the feed again from 0 up to the pull cursor and applies only the pending collections' events, one page per transaction with its own cursor (`resync_after`), so a failed attempt is resumed by the next call; the transaction that reaches the pull cursor marks them kept, then it pulls as usual. It waits for a running sync first. Other connections to the same file may sync, resync or reopen it meanwhile: each page starts at the stored re-pull cursor and is applied (in an IMMEDIATE transaction) only if that cursor and the pending set are unchanged, otherwise it is dropped and the re-pull goes on from the stored state (from 0 if the set was changed, or not at all if another connection finished it, in which case `resync()` simply succeeds); keeping the collections reads the pull cursor in the same transaction, so a sync elsewhere that pulled further extends the re-pull. A page that runs past the cursor is applied whole for the pending collections, since a sync on another connection may skip those events meanwhile; applying them again later changes nothing. The re-pull does not call change listeners, and while it runs the device's cursor on the server goes back (the server records the `after` of every pull) until the normal pull at its end.
- `MetaStore` gets the collection lists and the re-pull cursor (cursor parsing is shared with the pull cursor); `DocsStore.deleteCollection`.

Tests: `packages/client/test/sync/selectiveSync.test.ts` (skipped events and cursor, refused reads and writes, option validation, a re-pull interrupted by a failure and resumed, a re-pull racing a sync, a reopen with another set and a resync on other connections, a collection left out), `packages/client/test/e2e/selectiveSync.test.ts` (a tasks-only phone against the server, then notes added and re-pulled). README updated.
